status: Design only; no shared runner, verifier, worker or game source changed.

verified_interface_gap.native_protocol: Their frozen src/native/engine.c choose_setup() calls setup_random(), despite linking ai_deploy.c. Twelve actual setup responses across both policies, both orientations and three seeds were legal and retained in deployment-protocol-trace.json.
verified_interface_gap.actual_game: src/scenes/deploy.c:282 and src/scenes/play.c:869 call setup_ai(1); demo additionally calls setup_ai(0). ai_deploy.c selects validated Classic mixtures for Normal/Hard and protected random for Easy/optional rules.
verified_interface_gap.validated_mix: Normal Fortress/Evolved2/Evolved3 tickets 50/40/10%; Hard40/50/10%. The RNG rejection step gives exactly uniform ten-ticket probabilities.
verified_interface_gap.implication: Native protocol own-setup benchmarks of the current immutable IDs would measure protected random. Replacing setup_random with setup_ai silently would change those IDs and is disallowed.

proposed_immutable_versions.validated_deployment_candidate: New descriptive ID, same move policy, add observer/native define AI_POLICY_DEPLOYMENT and policy metadata deployment='protocol'. choose_setup() calls setup_ai only under that guard; default calls setup_random exactly as before.
proposed_immutable_versions.protected_random_control: Register a separate deployment-enabled control ID with deployment='protocol', identical move policy and default choose_setup implementation. If the runner explicitly supports legacy protocol control without editing old metadata, retaining the existing ID is also semantically valid; do not change an old registry entry.
proposed_immutable_versions.important: The deployment macro belongs to native observer defines, not teacher rollout defines. The teacher Python driver already forwards setup requests without arguments to its observer.

smallest_runner_extension.entry_point: tools/tournament.py run(...,setup_mode='referee'); CLI --setup-mode referee|policy-owned. Existing default preserves current generation, random draws and pairing exactly.
smallest_runner_extension.scope: In policy-owned mode the first participant chooses its own normalized army; the second participant, including DOS, retains a referee-generated opponent army. Do not call the original DOS setup generator or alter DOS knowledge.
generation: Keep the existing family RNG draws of armies A,B and move_seed so independent comparisons with equal tournament seeds retain equal planned opponent armies and move seeds.
Use B as the second participant's normalized referee army for both side orientations. A is deliberately unused in this mode but its draw preserves the scheduling RNG stream.

Derive a documented setup_seed from move_seed independently of policy ID. In a fresh isolated frozen first-participant process send Classic rules, canonical new red, its difficulty, setup_seed, then setup without arguments. No opponent setup, opponent public ranks or future results enter this request.
Validate the returned forty glyphs and freeze the exact setup response and selection transcript/hash in tournament artifacts before queuing either match.

Play first-red with setups (owned,B), then first-blue with setups (B,owned). Both games use the same move_seed. Actual match processes still receive seed,new,setup-string exactly as before, so setup-generation RNG is independent of move RNG.

A matched protected-random control and validated-mixture candidate must use this SAME mode, same B, same setup_seed and same move seeds. Do not compare their scores directly with the historical default-mode benchmark as if only own setup changed.

metadata.pairing: normalized armies follow participant identity across swapped sides
metadata.family_scope: second participant referee army only; no longer describes both armies
metadata.comparison: end-to-end own-deployment plus fixed move policy against a referee-deployed opponent
metadata.setup_rng: document exact seed derivation; separate setup-generation process and independent movement seeding
metadata.setup_records: artifact path/hash, one own response and one opponent army per pair, with selection seed and frozen policy/recipe hashes

pair_verification.location: tools/tournament_store.py verify(), current mismatched paired-round check near line200
pair_verification.legacy: Missing setup_mode or setup_mode='referee': retain same physical red_setup/blue_setup across policy swaps.
pair_verification.new_mode: Require identities swapped, equal family and move_seed, a.red_setup==b.blue_setup and a.blue_setup==b.red_setup. Additionally bind each army to the metadata setup_owner/opponent and verify both actual strings against the frozen per-pair setup artifact and legal inventory.
pair_verification.reject: Unknown setup mode, absent setup evidence, invalid glyphs, mismatched setup ownership, altered own/opponent army, unexpected participant or mismatched pair seed. Failed DOS games remain unscored legal-prefix evidence.

worker_and_qt.worker: desktop/worker.cpp already accepts explicit setups per job, loads exactly those into truth and engines, and contains no cross-game pairing assumptions. No worker protocol or game execution change is needed.
worker_and_qt.companion: desktop/desk.cpp reads each game's stored red_setup/blue_setup, so replay artwork, colors and orientation need no change. Add a short metadata label identifying 'Policy-owned deployment' versus 'Common referee armies' if UI currently presents comparison mode; avoid claiming the new score isolates move strength.
worker_and_qt.review: Use the ordinary Classic runner, portable fmtour, full Python/native replay verification and Qt capture for the first new-mode match.

minimum_verification: Compile default native observer against pre-edit source and require identical output/runtime when AI_POLICY_DEPLOYMENT is absent.
New guarded protocol setup for Normal produces only the three exact validated normalized layouts across both sides; Easy/optional behavior remains defined by setup_ai.
Same setup_seed and canonical orientation produce deterministic legal army independently of concealed opponent ranks; no enemy setup appears in selection transport.
Frozen new source, recipe, difficulty and deployment metadata registered before saved matches; old policy entries remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
Old pairing mode still verifies its previous physical-side invariant; new mode accepts participant-bound armies and rejects deliberately corrupted pairs and artifacts.
Matched candidate/control schedules retain equal DOS armies, move seeds, family/round blocks and setup-selection seeds.

historical_evidence.existing_deployment_research: 11,760 setup games retained in docs/ai-deployments/manifest.json. Validated Normal mixture improves protected random by2.74pp,95%[0.39,5.18]; Hard4.35pp[2.38,6.31], against five frozen native opponents. New individual evolved layouts did not reliably outperform the best existing Fortress.
historical_evidence.dos_development_associations: 420 historical development attempts,418 scored,29.78% overall; deployment-associations.json. Fully screened own Flags score22.41% versus31.72% unscreened overall, but within broad-mixed the association reverses65.63% versus30.68%. Both armies share family, so these are confounded descriptive associations, not evidence Bomb protection hurts or helps.
historical_evidence.miner_access: 396/420 own armies already give all five Miners a geometric front route after friendly mobile blockers move. Immediate front-row Miners show no consistent within-family association. This does not motivate a Miner-front-placement rule without a controlled setup experiment.

initial_experiment: First test the already validated production mixture against current protected-random protocol control, freezing the move policy and opponent armies. Only after that consider a setup optimizer fitted on designated DOS development games, with fresh final seeds and no opponent setup features.
